plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-13 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Geosciences program page (poid=10842) and its linked official degree map, 'Geosciences Degree Maps (2026-2027)', tab 'Geosciences (Campus)' (the workbook's only program tab; no Online tab exists), last updated/reviewed July 27, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. Per the catalog, all courses must be passed with a C (2.0) or better to be counted in the major, all prerequisite courses must be passed with C (2.0) or better, credits greater than 10 years old will not be accepted for this major, and some courses are taught every other year. Every semester's courses sum to the map's printed semester total (15/16/14/14/14/13/6 summer/14/14) and the plan to the catalog's printed Total Credits, BA Degree: 120. The map's nine terms include a Summer (3rd Year) term carrying GEO 4960 Field Geology (6 credits), transcribed as printed. The catalog's Geology Core (37 credits) is placed exactly: CHEM 1210/1215, GEO 1220/1225, GEO 3210/3215, GEO 3410/3415, GEO 3510/3515, GEO 4800, GEO 4960, MATH 1050 and MATH 1060 all appear in their map terms, and the Introductory Requirement (4 credits, one of seven lecture/lab pairings) is the map's Fall Year 1 introductory row, which prints no course number and is recorded as a choice slot carrying the seven pairings. The BA foreign-language requirement (16 credits) is the map's LANG 1010, LANG 1020, LANG 2010 and LANG 2020 rows (4 credits each, printed as GE Humanities). DISCLOSED MAP-VS-CATALOG BLOCK DIFFERENCES, transcribed as printed and not reconciled (Geology BS precedent, where the map's elective rows exceeded the catalog minimum): the map's three 4-credit 'Major Elective Course & Lab' rows plus the separately placed GEO 4999 Geosciences Seminar (1 credit, itself on the catalog's electives list) total 13 credits against the catalog's Geology Electives block of 11, and its six 3-credit 'Major Integrative Elective' rows total 18 against the catalog's Integrative Electives block of 15. The catalog's own block totals (BA Requirement 16 + General Education 28+ + Curriculum 67) exceed 120 if added naively because one semester of foreign language may also fulfill the GE Humanities requirement and several curriculum courses carry GE tags (the introductory pairing and CHEM 1210 as GE Physical Sciences, MATH 1050 and MATH 1060 as GE Quantitative Literacy); the map's placement is the university's own reconciliation to 120. Catalog course titles are recorded where the map shortens them (GEO 3410 Sedimentology and Stratigraphy; GEO 4999 Geosciences Seminar).

courses.title: Geology Introductory Course & Lab
courses.choice_note: Printed in the degree map as 'Geology Introductory Course & Lab* (GE Physical)' with no course number; the catalog's Introductory Requirement is Complete 4 credits from one of the following lecture/lab pairings: GEO 1010 Geology Introductory Survey 3 & GEO 1115 Fundamentals of Geology Lab 1; GEO 1030 Earthquakes, Volcanoes, and Natural Hazards 3 & GEO 1115 1; GEO 1040 Dinosaurs and the History of Life 3 & GEO 1115 1; GEO 1050 Geology of National Parks 3 & GEO 1055 Geology National Parks Lab 1; GEO 1090 How the Earth Works 3 & GEO 1095 How the Earth Works Lab 1; GEO 1110 Exploring Earth: Introduction to Geology 3 & GEO 1115 1; GEO 2210 Geology of Southern Utah 3 & GEO 2215 Geology of Southern Utah Lab 1.

courses.title: Major Integrative Elective
courses.choice_note: Printed in the degree map as 'Major Integrative Elective*'; the slot is one of the map's six 3-credit 'Major Integrative Elective' rows; the catalog's Integrative Electives block is Complete 15 credits from the listed courses in any of the areas (Agriculture/Range Management, Biology, Chemistry, Communication, Computer Science, English, Geography, Mathematics, Outdoor Recreation in Parks & Tourism, Physics), whose courses carry their own catalog credits (1-4; the variable-credit GEOG 4890 GIS Internship 2-8 is not carried in this slot's options because the slot is a fixed 3-credit row as printed on the map). The six map rows total 18 credits against the catalog block's 15 (see the plan notes).
